title: Data Factory: pipelines, datasets, linked services and integration runtime

videos.script: Every night at three, Quitanda's export has to become tomorrow's dashboard. Data Factory is what runs that night. {{night}} It does little of the work itself. It copies files, and it hands the rest to other services, in order. {{order}} A factory has six parts. A trigger starts a pipeline. The pipeline's activities read and write datasets. Each dataset names a linked service, and the linked service knows how to sign in. {{chain}} Underneath is the integration runtime, the machinery that does the copy. It decides which network the data crosses. {{runtime}} There is no emulator for any of this. So you will declare Quitanda's factory in Terraform, and check it on your laptop. {{declare}} You will see what the check catches, and the typo it lets through. {{typo}} Then the triggers. A clock, a window of time, or a file arriving. Each one means something different by last night. {{triggers}} And the bill, which charges for runs and minutes, and almost nothing for the factory itself. {{bill}}
